binders: An arbitrary finite index type ι.
An arbitrary measurable sample space Ω.
A probability measure μ on Ω.
A family of Boolean-valued functions B_i:Ω→Bool indexed by i∈ι.
hypotheses: The index cardinality n=|ι| is strictly positive.
Every B_i is measurable into Bool with its discrete measurable structure.
The indexed family (B_i) is jointly independent under μ.
For every i, the pushforward distribution of B_i under μ is Bernoulli with success probability 1/2.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001(b)=1 if b=true and LocalDef001(b)=0 otherwise.
LocalDef002 is the Bernoulli PMF on Bool with parameter 1/2, so true and false each have probability 1/2.
The probability P(A) is represented by the real value of μ(A).
All threshold comparisons use ≥, so equality at 3n/4 and at deviation n/4 is included.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any nonempty finite family of jointly independent fair Boolean random variables, encode true as 1 and false as 0 and let S be their sum. The probability that S is at least three quarters of the number of variables is at most the probability that S differs from half that number by at least one quarter of it, and this deviation probability is at most 4 divided by the number of variables.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition explicitly excludes the empty index set, ensuring that the denominator n in 4/n is nonzero.
The threshold quantities 3n/4, n/2, and n/4 are real numbers; there is no integer rounding.
The bound 4/n may exceed 1 for small positive n, making the second inequality valid but potentially uninformative in those cases.
Measure.real converts an extended-nonnegative measure to a real number; because μ is a probability measure, all event measures are finite and the conversion loses no information.
The conclusion is only the displayed pair of probability inequalities; it does not explicitly identify the distribution of S or assert a sharper tail estimate.
The finite sum of measurable 0-1 variables is measurable, so the events are ordinary measurable probability events rather than relying on nonmeasurable-set behavior.
